audit.whatIsWrong: Chart gave Sett levels 1 and 2 and downgraded 4-5 and first item to Skill.
audit.why: The mirror (nautilus__sett) settled Nautilus / Skill / Sett / Sett / Sett / Sett / Skill. Staggering Blow roots on his first attack on a target and Dredge Line reaches 1150, so level 1 is his; once Facebreaker and Grit are online the middle rows are Sett's.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 1, 3 and 5 flipped as matched full+content pairs with ratings.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level-6 spike claimed The Show Stopper counter-engages his Q or R initiation from range.
audit.why: The Show Stopper is 400 range on 120/100/80s — it does not gap-close. Depth Charge is 825 range and Dredge Line 1150, so he closes the distance and you answer once he arrives.
audit.corrected: spikes[1] and whys[4] now state the 400-range grab as an answer, not an initiation.

audit.whatIsWrong: Repeated claim that 'E into the wall stuns him', plus a warning about being Q-pulled 'into a wall stun'.
audit.why: Facebreaker stuns only when it catches enemies on OPPOSITE sides of Sett — terrain is irrelevant; a lone target is slowed. Riot's Dredge Line text says colliding with terrain pulls NAUTILUS toward it — that is his mobility, not a stun applied to you.
audit.corrected: whys[2], mid and spikes[0] now state the both-sides rule and drop the unsupported wall-stun claim.

audit.whatIsWrong: Cooldown panel listed Dredge Line twice with no numbers and never mentioned Titan's Wrath.
audit.why: Dredge Line is 14/13/12/11/10s at 1150 range; Titan's Wrath is a flat 12s shield at every rank, which is the real gate on your burst window.

edits.before: Sett wins Level 1 as Nautilus can't punish beyond one Dredge Line and loses the auto exchange.
edits.after: Nautilus wins Level 1: Staggering Blow roots on his first hit and Dredge Line reaches 1150.

edits.before: Sett stays ahead at Level 2 with Pit Grit trades that out-tempo his shield.
edits.after: Level 2 is skill: your Q double-punch against his 12s Titan's Wrath shield.

edits.before: Sett dominates Level 3 once E into the wall stuns Nautilus for a free Q-Haymaker.
edits.after: Sett dominates Level 3 once Facebreaker boxes him in for a free Q-Haymaker cash.

edits.before: Sett wins Level 6 because R counter-engages his Q or R and he has no escape.
edits.after: Sett wins Level 6: The Show Stopper grabs at 400 range and he has no dash out.

edits.before: Double-punch passive makes you the strongest level-1 auto-trader in the lane. Punish Nautilus on every CS, but respect his opening tool — chips now, all-ins later.
edits.after: Staggering Blow roots you on his first auto and Dredge Line reaches 1150, so level 1 is his. Farm the wave, bank the Grit his poke hands you, and wait for Facebreaker.

edits.before: With Q Knuckle Down and E Facebreaker you out-damage Nautilus in every trade; his Q Dredge Line only threatens you if you're standing near a wall, so fight in open lane and his shield-into-slow combo can't outpace your Grit.
edits.after: Q Knuckle Down and Facebreaker out-damage him in every trade, but Facebreaker only stuns with enemies on both sides — pull him across your wave. Dredge Line is 14s at rank 1, so a miss buys you a free window.

edits.before: R The Show Stopper flips any Nautilus engage: when he Q's or R's onto you, answer with your ult to slam him back and win the exchange since he has no mobility to reposition.
edits.after: The Show Stopper reaches only 400 units, so it answers his engage rather than starting one: let Dredge Line drag him to you, then grab and slam him away from his own minions.

edits.before: Levels 3-6 stay firmly yours. E into a wall stuns him for a free Q-Haymaker, and his W shield only blunts one trade before you reset Grit and go again. His CC chain is real, so fight away from terrain and don't let him Q-pull you into a wall stun.
edits.after: Levels 3-6 stay firmly yours. Pull him across your minions so Facebreaker stuns instead of slowing, then cash Haymaker. Titan's Wrath is a flat 12s shield that blunts one trade — bait it, reset Grit, and go again the moment it drops.

edits.before: - Nautilus Dredge Line (Hook): matchup-defining — His only engage. Dodge it. Track it before every engage. - Nautilus Dredge Line: Hurls an anchor; on a champ hit, pulls both together — his hook. Dodge or sidestep it.
edits.after: - Nautilus Dredge Line (Q, 1150 range, 14s at rank 1): matchup-defining hook that pulls you together — sidestep it, then commit. - Nautilus Titan's Wrath (W): a flat 12s shield; bait it out before you cash Haymaker.

notes: Dredge Line carries a 'terrain' derived flag, but Riot's text only says colliding with terrain pulls Nautilus toward it — no terrain is created, so the old 'fight in open lane or he wall-stuns you' framing was removed rather than restated. Whether Staggering Blow's root can be tenacity-reduced or cleansed is not in the kit text, so no claim was made. Sett's W range reads 25000 in the kit — a tooltip artifact, not used in any advice (same note as the mirror).
